name: C-17 Globemaster III
summary: Large four-engine strategic and tactical airlifter able to operate from short, rough runways; the backbone of USAF airlift.

wings: High-mounted swept wing with slight droop (anhedral)
Prominent flap-track fairings under the trailing edge
engines: Four turbofans on pylons under the wing
Engines fitted with large thrust reversers
fuselage: Wide, bulky fuselage with large landing-gear sponsons along the lower sides
Upswept rear fuselage with a cargo ramp and doors
Short blunt nose; usually dark grey
tail: T-tail: tall swept fin with the horizontal tail on top
Slight dihedral on the horizontal tail

tellTales: T-tail on a high-winged four-jet transport
Bulky gear sponsons along the lower fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The C-17 is shorter and stockier with winglets and gear sponsons; the C-5 is much longer, has no winglets and a large rounded visor nose.
The C-17 is a four-jet with a T-tail and winglets; the C-130J has propellers and a conventional tail.
